title: Tasks, events, Chatter, email integration, calendar integration, and Salesforce mobile
objectives: Distinguish Task (due-dated to-do) from Event (start/end calendar block) as Activity records related to people and deals.
Place Chatter as the in-org feed and groups product, not as email and not as Knowledge.
Explain email and calendar integration as sync/compose bridges to the Activity timeline, not as a second CRM.
State what Salesforce mobile is for (on-the-go Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, Tasks, Events) without inventing offline limits.
diagnostic_question: A seller wants calls logged, a meeting on a shared calendar, a deal discussion visible to the account team, Outlook compose with logging, and phone updates at the airport. Which of Task, Event, Chatter, email integration, calendar integration, or Salesforce mobile do you pick for each, and what would you refuse to fake with a custom object?
definition: Productivity layer on top of APP-001 records: Tasks are to-dos with due dates; Events are calendar blocks with start and end; both appear on the activity timeline. Chatter is the internal feed, groups, and @mentions product. Email and calendar integration connect Outlook/Gmail/calendar to Salesforce so messages and meetings can log as activities. The Salesforce mobile app lets sellers track and update accounts, contacts, leads, and opportunities, make calls, send emails, and act on upcoming tasks and events while away from the desktop. ([Salesforce Help Sales / mobile](https://help.salesforce.com/s/products/sales); [Stage/forecast mapping still uses Activities as work evidence](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail people who create a custom Meeting object, who treat Chatter as email, who think Salesforce mobile is a different data model, or who add Opportunity Stages to track calls (APP-002). Duplicate meetings from calendar sync and unlogged emails are the production pain.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a newsroom. A Task is an assignment on the reporter's list with a due time. An Event is a live broadcast slot with a start and end. Chatter is the newsroom wall—@mentions and group threads, not the wire service. Email integration is the correspondent's mailbox that can file a copy on the story. Calendar integration is the studio booking board. Salesforce mobile is the reporter's phone in the field, updating the same stories—not a second newsroom.
deeper_explanation: Tasks and Events are Activities related to Who (Lead/Contact) and What (Account, Opportunity, Case, and other WhatId targets). A Task has a due date and status; an Event has StartDateTime and EndDateTime. Neither is a Chatter post. APP-002 already warned: do not invent Stages to mean 'we called them.'

Chatter is collaboration in the org: record feeds, groups, @mentions. It is not Knowledge publication (APP-004), not Files libraries (APP-006), and not Outlook. Feed tracking is metadata; posts are data.

Email integration (Outlook/Gmail integrations, Lightning Email, Einstein Activity Capture as a neighboring product) exists so sellers can send or log email against records. Do not invent capture-delay minutes. Calendar integration creates or syncs Events; double-booking and private-event behavior are Needs verification per the connector in the org.

Salesforce Help describes a seller-focused mobile experience: track and update accounts, contacts, leads, and opportunities; make calls; send emails; see and act on upcoming tasks and events in the activity timeline. Compact layouts and mobile navigation are metadata. The app is not a separate database. ([Sales Help hub](https://help.salesforce.com/s/products/sales))

Einstein Copilot and Inbox are mentioned on the Sales Help hub as adjacent productivity; this lesson does not claim their licensing. Offline mobile behavior, exact Outlook add-in names, and EAC vs manual logging: Needs verification in the target org.

mental_model.analogy: A newsroom: Task = assignment on the list, Event = broadcast slot with start/end, Chatter = the wall, email integration = correspondent mailbox filing a copy, calendar integration = studio booking board, Salesforce mobile = field reporter phone on the same stories.
useful_mapping: Activity timeline → the story's work history
Chatter post → internal wall thread, not a Task
Email logged → often a Task of type Email (product-dependent)
Salesforce mobile → same objects, compact layouts
Custom Meeting object → usually the wrong newsroom
where_it_breaks: Some email products log as EmailMessage, not Task—do not swear it is always a Task.
Chatter files vs Salesforce Files (APP-006) overlap in UX.
Mobile offline drafts may exist; do not invent conflict rules.
The analogy does not encode sharing of private events or legal hold.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Tasks are due-dated to-dos. Events are start/end meetings. Chatter is the internal wall. Email and calendar integrations log work onto records. Salesforce mobile updates the same Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, Tasks, and Events—not a second CRM. Do not fake calls with a new Stage.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I refuse a custom Meeting object unless there is a true data-model gap. I relate Activities via Who and What. I keep Knowledge and Files in their topics. Lead Settings still own Lead capture defaults.

terminology.plain: A to-do with a due date and status, related to a person and/or a record.
terminology.precise: Activity subtype. Status/Priority/DueDate. Appears on the activity timeline. Not an Event and not a Chatter post.
terminology.example: Task LAB_Call Maya due tomorrow, related to Lead LAB_Maya.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Event: has start and end, not just due date.
terminology.boundary: Recurring tasks and series: reverify in current Help.

terminology.plain: A meeting or appointment with a start and end time.
terminology.precise: Activity subtype on the calendar and timeline. Calendar integration often creates these. Invitees may be Contacts/Leads/Users depending on product.
terminology.example: Event LAB_Discovery 10:00–10:30 related to Opportunity LAB_Northwind Q3.
terminology.boundary: Private events and Group Events: Needs verification per edition.

terminology.plain: The in-Salesforce feed: posts, comments, @mentions, groups.
terminology.precise: Collaboration product on records and groups. Not email, not Knowledge, not a Task. Feed tracking is metadata.
terminology.example: @mention AE on Account LAB_Northwind feed about legal review.
terminology.non_example: An Outlook email to the account team with no Salesforce log.
terminology.boundary: Chatter vs Slack Salesforce integrations are neighboring.

terminology.plain: Connecting Outlook or Gmail so sellers can send/log email on Salesforce records.
terminology.precise: A family of products (Lightning Email, add-ins, EAC). Logs work onto the timeline. Not a second CRM. Exact object written (Task vs EmailMessage) is product-specific.
terminology.example: Seller sends from Outlook with LAB_Northwind Opportunity selected to log.
terminology.non_example: Forwarding customer mail to a personal inbox with no logging.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Email-to-Case (APP-003): service capture, not seller productivity.

terminology.plain: Syncing or creating Salesforce Events from Outlook/Google calendar.
terminology.precise: Keeps meeting blocks aligned. Risk: duplicates if two syncs fight. Not Tasks.
terminology.example: Outlook appointment with Contact LAB_Maya creates Event on the Contact.
terminology.non_example: A Task due at 10:00 used as the meeting.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Salesforce calendar UI without an external connector.
terminology.boundary: Which direction syncs, and private events: Needs verification.

terminology.plain: The official phone app that uses the same CRM records.
terminology.precise: Help: update accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities; calls; emails; upcoming tasks and events on the activity timeline. Compact layouts and navigation are metadata.
terminology.example: AE updates Opportunity Amount in the airport using the mobile app.
terminology.non_example: A spreadsheet on the phone treated as offline CRM.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Experience Cloud mobile site for customers.
terminology.boundary: Offline, branding, and Mobile Publisher: neighboring.

terminology.plain: The chronological work history on a record.
terminology.precise: Shows Tasks, Events, and logged emails (as configured). Mobile Help calls out acting on upcoming tasks and events here.
terminology.example: Opportunity LAB_Northwind Q3 timeline shows discovery Event and follow-up Task.
terminology.non_example: A report of all Tasks in the org.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Chatter feed: collaboration, can be adjacent on the page.
terminology.boundary: Timeline filters and EAC captured activities: product-specific.

terminology.plain: The handful of fields mobile (and some highlights) show first.
terminology.precise: Metadata on the object. Changing it is not a mobile app install. Does not change sharing.
terminology.example: Contact compact layout: Name, Phone, Email, Account.
terminology.non_example: A page layout with 80 fields expected to be usable on a phone.
terminology.boundary: Dynamic forms on mobile: Needs verification.

when_to_use: When a seller must log a due-dated Task or a start/end Event on a Lead, Contact, Account, Opportunity, or Case.
When the account team needs Chatter discussion rather than an email-only side thread.
When Outlook or Gmail should log email or calendar meetings onto the Salesforce activity timeline.
When sellers need Salesforce mobile to update the same accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, tasks, and events in the field.
when_not_to_use: Do not create a custom Meeting object to replace Event, or a new Opportunity Stage to mean a Task was completed.
Do not use Chatter as Knowledge (APP-004) or as Email-to-Case (APP-003).
Do not treat Salesforce mobile as a different data model or a substitute for compact layouts.
Do not run two email-capture products without a duplicate plan, or promise Einstein Activity Capture details without reading that product's Help.

interview_questions.question: Task versus Event versus Chatter?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A Task is a due-dated to-do. An Event is a start/end meeting. Chatter is the internal feed. All can sit on the same Account, but only Tasks and Events are Activities on the timeline.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I relate Activities with Who and What. I will not replace Events with a custom object if sellers also need Outlook and mobile. I will not use Chatter as a to-do list because it has no due-date assignment model like Task. Knowledge remains APP-004.
interview_questions.example: Call Maya = Task on Lead; discovery = Event on Opportunity; legal = Chatter on Account.

interview_questions.question: What does Salesforce mobile change?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The form factor and compact layouts—not the objects. Help says sellers update accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities and act on tasks and events on the timeline.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I configure mobile navigation and compact layouts. I do not promise a separate mobile database. Offline, branding, and MDM are neighboring. Lead Settings still apply to Leads updated from the phone. I keep page layouts from dumping 80 fields onto a handset.
interview_questions.example: Same Opportunity Id edited at the airport; Amount matches desktop.
weak_answer_warnings: Saying mobile is a different org

interview_questions.question: Sellers live in Outlook and skip Salesforce after meetings.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Calendar integration for Events, email integration for logged mail, plus mobile for updates. Do not invent a Meeting__c. Do not use Email-to-Case.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I identify the licensed connector. I pilot with LAB_ addresses. I watch duplicates if EAC plus an add-in both log. I train WhatId selection so mail lands on the Opportunity. I still want a Task for follow-ups that are not meetings.
interview_questions.example: Outlook appointment with Contact Maya creates Event; follow-up Task due Friday.

interview_questions.question: Ops wants a custom Meeting object because Event cannot store LAB_Room__c.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I add a custom field on Event first. A new object drops off standard timeline, mobile activity, and calendar connectors.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If they need a complex room-scheduling product, that is a different app (maybe AppExchange—APP-007), not a reason to abandon Activity. I show Help's mobile timeline expectation. I refuse to break Who/What reporting.
interview_questions.example: Event.LAB_Room__c on the discovery Event; still related to Opportunity.
tradeoffs: Field on Event vs new object

interview_questions.question: Mobile users say 'Salesforce is empty' but desktop is not.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Same sharing, different navigation and compact layouts. Check app menu, offline, and whether they are in the right org.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I verify username/org. I check Salesforce mobile navigation items. I check compact layout and FLS. I do not rebuild sharing first if desktop list views work for that user. I confirm they are not in an Experience Cloud site.
interview_questions.example: Opportunities tab missing from mobile navigation; desktop has it in Sales app.
follow_ups: Profiles vs permission sets for mobile?

interview_questions.question: Every Outlook send creates two Tasks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Two loggers. Identify Lightning Email, add-in, and EAC. Turn one off for a LAB_ user and retest.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at created-by and timestamps. I do not delete the Task object. I check whether one record is EmailMessage and one is Task—Needs verification per product. I document the surviving logger.
interview_questions.example: EAC plus manual Outlook add-in both on; two timeline rows per send.

interview_questions.question: When would you not enable calendar sync?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When sellers already double-book, when private personal calendars must not enter CRM, or when a pilot already produced duplicate Events.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I might keep Salesforce Events without bidirectional sync. I might log meetings manually or via an add-in 'save to Salesforce' without full sync. Privacy and duplicate risk beat convenience. Mobile still shows Events that exist in Salesforce.
interview_questions.example: Executives with mixed personal/work calendars: no org-wide sync; AE cohort only.

interview_questions.question: Teach this with the newsroom analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Assignment list is Task, broadcast slot is Event, wall is Chatter, correspondent mailbox is email integration, studio board is calendar, field phone is Salesforce mobile on the same stories.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: It breaks when logged email is EmailMessage not Task, when Chatter files collide with Files, when mobile offline conflicts, and when Email-to-Case is the service wire not the correspondent mailbox. I cite Help's mobile object list and the Stage-mapping reason not to invent Called stages. Lead Settings still own Lead defaults.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard: one Opportunity story with Task, Event, Chatter, mobile edit.
weak_answer_warnings: Generic catalog metaphors instead of the newsroom mapping
